signals.entity: European Commission - EUDI Wallet Architecture and Reference Framework (ARF)
signals.signal: ARF v3.0.0 released 23/07/2026 on the Commission's own eu-digital-identity-wallet GitHub - the first major ARF version since v2.9.0 (21/05/2025). It re-bases the ARF on the 2026 amending Commission Implementing Regulations (PID = person identification data, EAA = electronic attestation of attributes, security, ecosystem notifications, protocols, Wallet-Relying-Party registration); adds 'Relying Party Services' and wallet-to-wallet interaction; requires retrieval of BOTH Trusted Lists and Lists of Trusted Entities; and - the operationally decisive part - adds a Functional Conformance Assessment Framework with reusable test cases published at conformance.eudi.dev. The ARF is the binding technical blueprint every wallet provider and every wallet-relying party (RP) builds to.
signals.implies: For the first time bank-side wallet acceptance is objectively testable before the 24/12/2027 Art.5f(2) duty. Printec must re-base the Namirial digital onboarding/eKYC stack on ARF 3.0.0 (SD-JWT VC + ISO/IEC mdoc credential formats, RP access/registration certificates, OpenID4VP presentation) with Thales HSM custody of RP private keys, and package an 'EUDI wallet acceptance readiness assessment' for Alpha Bank, Erste Croatia, BCR, Bank of Cyprus, OTP/Raiffeisen Albania.
signals.likelihood: High - published and conformance tooling live; RP build work must run through 2027
signals.followup: Pull the ARF 3.0.0 Relying Party chapter and the conformance.eudi.dev test catalogue; map each test to a Namirial/Thales component; watch for ARF 3.1 before 24/12/2026.

signals.signal: Full text now obtained (EUR-Lex is WAF-blocked to direct fetch; retrieved via a reader proxy over the EUR-Lex HTML). CIR (EU) 2026/1731 of 15/07/2026 amends Implementing Regulations (EU) 2024/2977 (PID and EAA), 2024/2979 (wallet integrity and core functionalities), 2024/2980 (ecosystem notifications) and 2024/2982 (protocols and interfaces) 'as regards applicable standards and specifications'; it enters into force on the 20th day after OJ publication (OJ 22/07/2026 -> 11/08/2026, matching the baseline). SUBSTANCE THE BASELINE DID NOT HAVE: (a) new Art.3a - a wallet unit must WARN the user that a request involves sharing BIOMETRIC data whenever a portrait is disclosed, and take explicit confirmation; portrait inclusion in the PID becomes MANDATORY only from 11/08/2028 (a new, previously unrecorded deadline); (b) new Art.14a - an official EU Digital Identity Wallet TRUST MARK with prescribed visual/technical characteristics (Pantone 661 and 116, minimum 64 x 85 px at 150 dpi) that wallet units must display; (c) new Annex Ia - mandatory cryptographic mechanisms; new Annex Ib - wallet unit attestation (WUA) technical requirements; (d) gatekeepers must enable CTAP 2.3 local communication channels for device authentication in cross-device flows; (e) PID encoding updated in both ISO/IEC-mdoc and SD-JWT VC, with W3C VCDM support once profiles exist.
signals.implies: Two concrete build items for Printec's eKYC/onboarding line: the biometric-portrait warning + explicit consent flow (a UX and DPIA change in any bank flow that requests a portrait from a wallet), and the trust-mark/WUA verification logic on the RP side. The 11/08/2028 mandatory-portrait date means banks CANNOT assume a portrait is available from a wallet before then - so document-plus-selfie remote identity proofing (Namirial) remains necessary alongside wallet acceptance, not replaced by it. The biometric-data and consent points are a data-protection question: Printec's DPO / Compliance team must be consulted before any customer-facing interpretation.
signals.followup: Obtain the signed OJ PDF to confirm Art.3a/14a numbering and the 11/08/2028 portrait date verbatim; brief the DPO on the biometric-warning obligation.

signals.signal: CIR (EU) 2026/798 of 07/04/2026 lays down reference standards and specifications for REMOTE ONBOARDING of users to EU Digital Identity Wallets. It permits onboarding on an electronic identification means at assurance level 'substantial' PROVIDED it is combined with additional remote onboarding procedures so that the combination meets assurance level 'high'. The Annex adapts ETSI TS 119 461 V2.1.1 (2025-02) - the identity-proofing standard already used for qualified trust services - naming the applicable clauses on operational risk assessment, identity-proofing service management, attended and unattended remote identity-proofing use cases, and the enhancement procedures from baseline to extended identity assurance. Wallet providers must apply data protection by design and by default (GDPR Art.25), especially for biometric data, and must give sufficient explanations and remedies on failure plus a route for users to exercise data-subject rights including rectification and contesting a decision. Entry into force / application: 20th day after OJ publication. This was the missing implementing act that had blocked remote wallet enrolment; the baseline did not carry it.
signals.implies: The most directly monetisable eIDAS-2 act for Printec: it makes ETSI TS 119 461 remote identity proofing the legal on-ramp to the wallet in all ten EU footprint markets. That is precisely the Namirial digital onboarding/eKYC product, with IMTF Siron / FICO behind it for the AML/CDD (customer due diligence) leg. Buyers: national wallet providers AND any bank that will issue or consume attestations. WHO: significant institutions in AT/BG/HR/CY/GR/SI/SK plus RO/HU/CZ nationals. WHAT: a TS 119 461-conformant identity-proofing service and its audit evidence. WHEN BUDGET COMMITS: now to H1-2027, 6-12 months ahead of the 24/12/2027 acceptance duty. Data-subject-rights wording here is a DPO/Compliance question, not one to rule on commercially.
signals.likelihood: High - in force since April 2026 and a precondition for any wallet launching before 24/12/2026
signals.followup: Confirm Namirial's ETSI TS 119 461 V2.1.1 conformance attestation and whether it covers the unattended use case; get the OJ PDF for the exact publication date.

signals.entity: European Commission - Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/848 (registration of wallet-relying parties)
signals.signal: CIR (EU) 2025/848 of 06/05/2025 on the registration of wallet-relying parties APPLIES FROM 24/12/2026 - the same day as the Art.5a(1) wallet-provision deadline. From that date a relying party (which expressly includes banks and PSPs) may only interact with a wallet unit if it is entered in its Member State's national register of wallet-relying parties, has declared its entitlements and whether it will rely on electronic identification of natural persons, keeps its entries updated without undue delay, and requests only the minimum necessary attributes. Registered parties are then issued Wallet-Relying-Party ACCESS CERTIFICATES (which authenticate the RP to the wallet unit) and optionally REGISTRATION CERTIFICATES (which state which attributes the RP may request, as an anti-oversharing control). The Regulation sets no explicit deadline for Member States to stand the registers up - only that they must exist before application - which is the practical risk in the footprint.
signals.implies: This is the FIRST hard EU date that bites on banks themselves - a year earlier than the widely-quoted 24/12/2027 acceptance duty. Banks in all ten EU footprint markets need: (a) a registration filing and an entitlement/attribute-minimisation policy, (b) RP access-certificate key material - Thales HSM / PCI, (c) an RP endpoint that presents access and registration certificates and enforces attribute minimisation - Namirial onboarding/eKYC plus integration services, (d) evidence for the supervisor. BUDGET MUST COMMIT Q4-2025 to mid-2026 for a 24/12/2026 date, i.e. this is already late; the realistic sell is a fast-follow remediation package in H2-2026 / H1-2027.
signals.likelihood: High - date is on the face of the Regulation
signals.followup: For each of AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, GR, HU, RO, SK, SI, identify the designated national registrar of wallet-relying parties and whether the register is actually live; that gap list is the sales map.

signals.entity: Republic of Austria - Federal Chancellery / State Secretary for Digitalisation Alexander Proell
signals.signal: CARRIED DEBT CLOSED. At the National Council Budget Committee on 29/06/2026, State Secretary Proell stated on the record that NO EU member state will have implemented the EUDI Wallet requirements by end-2026 ('Kein einziges EU-Mitglied werde bis Ende 2026 die Vorgaben der EUDI-Wallet umgesetzt haben'), and that Austria will implement them INCREMENTALLY. He reported roughly 6 million activated ID Austria identities and work on usability. Federal Chancellery budget: EUR 652.6m for 2027 (+EUR 103.5m) and EUR 660.5m for 2028, with digitalisation up EUR 39.9m (2027) and EUR 5.3m (2028). Separately, parliamentary question 6289/J of 12/06/2026 on the introduction of the EUDI Wallet was answered on 12/08/2026 (5687/AB) by Interior Minister Karner with a single line - the questions 'fall outside the remit of the Federal Ministry of the Interior' - i.e. no Austrian ministry publicly owns the wallet file in answer to Parliament. Austria's building blocks are ID Austria (eIDAS-notified since 2022) and the eAusweise app (mDL and other credentials, built by youniqx Identity AG, a subsidiary of the Austrian State Printing House OeSD).
signals.source_name: Parlament Oesterreich - Parlamentskorrespondenz PK0644 (Budgetausschuss, 29/06/2026); Anfragebeantwortung 5687/AB of 12/08/2026 to 6289/J
signals.implies: Austria - an SSM market (Erste Group, Raiffeisen Bank International, BAWAG, UniCredit Bank Austria) - will reach 24/12/2026 with a partial, incrementally-delivered wallet built on ID Austria/eAusweise rather than a certified EUDI Wallet. This SHIFTS rather than removes Printec's opportunity: the bank-side duties (RP registration from 24/12/2026 under CIR 2025/848; acceptance from 24/12/2027 under Art.5f(2)) are NOT suspended because a national provider slips. Austrian banks therefore face a compressed 2027 integration window. Pitch a wallet-agnostic acceptance layer (Namirial eKYC + RP middleware + Thales HSM) that works against ID Austria/eAusweise now and the certified wallet later. Budget must commit H1-2027.
signals.likelihood: High - stated by the responsible State Secretary in committee
signals.followup: Track the Austrian E-GovG / E-ID-G amendment designating the wallet provider and the national certification scheme and CAB; ask whether FMA/OeNB has said anything to banks about RP registration.

signals.entity: Republic of Croatia - Ministry of Justice, Administration and Digital Transformation (MPUDT)
signals.signal: CARRIED DEBT PARTLY CLOSED. Primary (gov.hr): Croatia migrated its national Trusted List to the TLv6 format on 29/04/2026 as required by the European Commission, which unblocked registration of NEW trust services on the Croatian Trusted List; MPUDT is the supervisory body for trust service providers. On the wallet itself there is still NO Croatian primary timetable: the only dated statement is from Igor Ljubi, head of division at the Croatian digital-transformation ministry, who put issuance of a CERTIFIED Croatian EUDI Wallet at Q4 2026 and named the certification scheme as the binding constraint - 'if there's no scheme, there is no wallet' - which is PRESS-tier (Biometric Update, Oct-2025), not a government publication. Croatia's base is NIAS (National Identification and Authentication System): 7 credentials at 2014 launch, 29 by 2025 (8 high, 17 substantial, 4 low), eIDAS node since 2017, eID/NIAS notified 2018; Certilia has 350,000+ users and 11m+ qualified remote signatures.
signals.source_name: gov.hr - Usluge povjerenja (trust services), Croatian Trusted List TLv6 migration; secondary: Biometric Update (press)
signals.implies: TLv6 is a hard prerequisite for qualified electronic attestation of attributes (QEAA) providers to appear on the Croatian Trusted List - the trust layer Croatian banks will consume. Erste&Steiermaerkische (an existing Printec OptiCash reference), Zagrebacka/UniCredit, PBZ/Intesa, OTP Croatia and RBA all need an RP integration plus a QEAA consumption path and RP registration by 24/12/2026. Printec route: Namirial eKYC/QEAA plus Thales HSM for RP and QTSP key custody. Sell on the completed TLv6 step rather than waiting for the wallet.
signals.likelihood: Medium - TLv6 confirmed primary; the Q4-2026 certified-wallet date is press-only and at risk on Ljubi's own certification-scheme point
signals.followup: Get a Croatian PRIMARY wallet timetable from MPUDT news and the NPOO C2.3 'Digitalna transformacija drustva i javne uprave' milestone reporting; establish whether a Croatian wallet certification scheme and conformity assessment body have been designated, and who will run the Croatian register of wallet-relying parties.

signals.entity: Republic of North Macedonia - Ministry for Digital Transformation / Sobranie
signals.signal: Primary bill text obtained. The Government bill amending the Law on Electronic Documents, Electronic Identification and Trusted Services (Predlog na zakon za izmenuvanje i dopolnuvanje na Zakonot za elektronski dokumenti, elektronska identifikacija i doverlivi uslugi) transposes eIDAS 2 and creates the 'digital wallet for electronic identity' (digitalen paricnik za elektronski identitet). Art.27: the law enters into force on the 8th day after gazette publication 'a ke otpocne da se primenuva od 1 juni 2027 godina' [and shall start to apply from 1 June 2027]. NEW DETAIL THE BASELINE DID NOT HAVE: Art.20-m(2) is a direct mirror of eIDAS Art.5f - private-sector relying parties, excluding micro and small enterprises, that require strong user authentication for online identification for a contractual obligation, EXPRESSLY INCLUDING 'bankarstvo, finansiski uslugi' [banking, financial services], MUST on the user's request enable use of European digital identity wallets registered in the registers of certified wallets. Art.20-lj puts the safekeeping duty on the wallet user. Implementing bylaws due within 6 months of entry into force (Art.25). Fiscal note: MKD 200,000,000 for 2026 and MKD 200,000,000 for 2027 (~EUR 3.25m each) for wallet implementation. The European Commission's North Macedonia Report 2025 independently confirms the Law 'was amended to transpose the eIDAS 2.0 Regulation and to introduce the Digital Identity Wallet', while noting existing e-ID/e-signature tools are 'still not user friendly and not free of cost for citizens' and that full alignment is not yet achieved.
signals.source_name: Government of RNM, Predlog na zakon (Ministry for Digital Transformation, June 2025, published by the Economic Chamber of North Macedonia); European Commission, North Macedonia Report 2025 (04/11/2025)
signals.implies: North Macedonia becomes the FIRST non-EU footprint market with a statutory bank duty to accept an EU-style identity wallet, from 01/06/2027 - six months BEFORE the EU's own 24/12/2027 Art.5f(2) date. WHO: Komercijalna Banka, Stopanska Banka Skopje (NBG), NLB Banka Skopje, Halkbank AD Skopje, ProCredit, Sparkasse Bank Makedonija, UNIBanka. WHAT: an RP acceptance/verification layer plus remote identity proofing - Namirial digital onboarding/eKYC, IMTF Siron for the CDD/AML leg, Thales HSM for RP keys, plus integration and managed services. WHEN BUDGET COMMITS: H2-2026 to H1-2027 (6-12 months ahead) - i.e. now; the 6-month bylaw window after entry into force is the moment to shape technical requirements with the Ministry.
signals.likelihood: High - primary bill text carries the date and the banking clause; EC confirms the transposing amendment was adopted
signals.followup: Confirm the ADOPTED gazette text and number (Sluzben vesnik na RSM br. 135 of 04/07/2025 is the likely vehicle; portal.mdt.gov.mk and ener.gov.mk were network-unreachable from this environment) and that Art.20-m and the 01/06/2027 application date survived unchanged; then track the 6-month bylaws and any NBRM guidance to banks.

signals.entity: Bosnia and Herzegovina - IDDEEA / Council of Ministers / Republika Srpska
signals.signal: The European Commission's BiH Report 2025 states flatly, in the financial-services chapter, that 'There is no legal and regulatory framework for digital identity, and banks can only offer hybrid solutions', and in the digital chapter that 'No progress was made in adopting a Law on electronic identity and trust services for electronic transactions in line with the EU acquis', with the standing EU recommendation to establish a SINGLE countrywide supervisory body and no progress on countrywide e-signature interoperability. LIVE 2026 DEVELOPMENTS (press-tier, Detektor/Radio Slobodna Evropa): Republika Srpska adopted its own entity Law on Electronic Identification, Digital Identity, E-Signature, E-Seal and Trust Services in JUNE 2026, creating an entity-level identity system with its own registers and certificate issuance; in MARCH 2026 the BiH Constitutional Court found provisions of the RS Law on Police unconstitutional insofar as they cover digital signing, issuance of qualified digital certificates and document personalisation, which are state-level competences; IDDEEA director Almir Badnjevic wrote to the Peace Implementation Council in June 2026 arguing the fragmentation threatens the state infrastructure, and a state minister publicly opposed transferring the competence to the entities on 23/06/2026. The state-level Prijedlog Zakona o elektronskoj identifikaciji i uslugama povjerenja za elektronske transakcije BiH is with the Council of Ministers in regular procedure, flagged as an 'important law for EU integration', but is NOT adopted. There is therefore NO BiH remote-eID law in force.
signals.source_name: European Commission, Bosnia and Herzegovina Report 2025 (04/11/2025); javnarasprava.ba draft-law record; Detektor (press, 28/06/2026)
signals.implies: Closes the 'BiH remote-eID law' question in the negative: there is no state framework, the entity-level RS law is contested at the Constitutional Court, and BiH banks (Raiffeisen BiH, UniCredit BiH, Intesa Sanpaolo Banka BiH, NLB, Sparkasse Bank BiH, ASA Banka, ProCredit) can only run 'hybrid' - i.e. partly branch-based - onboarding. That is a NEGATIVE for pure eID-dependent products but a POSITIVE for Printec's branch and self-service lines: as long as identity cannot be proven fully remotely, the physical channel stays load-bearing - bank kiosks and assisted-onboarding stations, NCR intelligent-deposit/recycling ATMs, and Namirial deployed in an ATTENDED (branch-assisted, ETSI TS 119 461 attended use case) configuration rather than unattended. Do NOT sell a remote-only eKYC roadmap into BiH this cycle.
signals.likelihood: Medium - state law adoption in the next 6-12 months is uncertain given the entity dispute
signals.followup: Track the Council of Ministers / Parliamentary Assembly calendar for the state Law on electronic identification and trust services, and the Constitutional Court challenge to the June-2026 RS law; ask CBBH and the two entity banking agencies what identification method they will accept for remote account opening.

signals.entity: Kosovo - Government / Agency for Information Society; e-Kosova
signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2025] The European Commission's Kosovo Report 2025 records that Kosovo ADOPTED the Law on electronic identification and trust services in electronic transactions (alongside the Law on cyber security), that a national electronic identification (eID) system became operational in 2024 on the e-Kosova platform (230 online services), and that 'The deployment of the government's national eID and eWallet is progressing with the launch of the piloting phase'. The Commission's recommendation is that 'Kosovo should ensure alignment with the new EU Digital Identity Framework' - i.e. the adopted law tracks eIDAS 1, not eIDAS 2, and a further alignment amendment is expected. No date is published for the eWallet's move from pilot to production.
signals.implies: Kosovo is the most advanced non-EU footprint market on state eID after Ukraine: a law is in force and a national eID plus eWallet is in pilot. For Printec that makes Kosovo the best non-EU candidate for a remote-onboarding play - Namirial eKYC bound to the national eID for Banka per Biznes, BKT Kosove, NLB Banka Kosove, ProCredit Kosovo, Raiffeisen Kosovo and TEB - and it pairs with the only other firm Kosovo trigger, the November-2026 Western Balkans TIPS-Clone onboarding window. Budget conversation now, ahead of a 2027 eWallet production date.
signals.likelihood: Medium - pilot is running but no production date is published
signals.followup: Get the Kosovo Law on electronic identification and trust services from gzk.rks-gov.net (Official Gazette) with its number and date, and ask CBK whether the national eID is accepted as a standalone CDD identification method for remote account opening.

signals.entity: Ukraine - National Bank of Ukraine / Ministry of Digital Transformation (Diia)
signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2025, with a live banking hook] The European Commission's Ukraine Report 2025 records that the Diia platform confirmed in 2023 that it meets or exceeds the relevant requirements of the eIDAS Regulation, and that the operator of the eIDAS NODE in Ukraine obtained ISO/IEC 27001 certification in JUNE 2025 - the two steps that precede EU recognition of Ukrainian eID. On the banking side, in FEBRUARY 2025 the NBU Board adopted a resolution enhancing regulation of cybersecurity, information security and ELECTRONIC TRUST SERVICES OVERSIGHT in the banking system, and NBU open-banking regulations adopted for the 01/08/2025 entry into force of Chapter 4 of the Law on Payment Services expressly set requirements on ELECTRONIC TRUST SERVICES for PSPs seeking account access. Ukraine also participates in the EU large-scale wallet pilots alongside the 26 Member States, Norway and Iceland.
signals.implies: Ukraine already has the deepest working remote-eID stack in the footprint (Diia + eIDAS node) and, uniquely among non-EU markets, an NBU rule tying electronic trust services to PSP authorisation. For Printec the sell is not eID creation but the AROUND-eID layer at banks: IMTF Siron / FICO for AML-CDD on Diia-verified identities, INETCO transaction monitoring, and Thales HSM/PCI for trust-service key custody - alongside the already-live NBU cyber resolution No.143 obligations biting 13/12/2026. PrivatBank is an existing NCR recycler reference to lead with.
signals.likelihood: Medium - eIDAS-node recognition timing depends on EU accession-track decisions
signals.followup: Retrieve the February-2025 NBU Board resolution on cybersecurity/information security/electronic trust services from bank.gov.ua with a desktop User-Agent and confirm its number and its trust-service clauses; check whether Ukraine's eIDAS node has been formally peer-reviewed.

signals.entity: Republic of Serbia - Government / RATEL; NBS
signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2025] The European Commission's Serbia Report 2025 recommends that in the coming year Serbia should 'further align its electronic communications, digital trust and cybersecurity legislation with the EU regulatory framework, including the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, eIDAS 2.0, the NIS2 Directive, and the Artificial Intelligence Act'. Serbia's framework remains the Law on Electronic Document, Electronic Identification and Trust Services in Electronic Business (eIDAS-1 aligned). NO eIDAS-2 transposition bill and no national wallet programme was identified for Serbia in this run.
signals.implies: No wallet-driven spend trigger in Serbia this cycle. Serbian banks (Raiffeisen Serbia - an existing Printec x-core reference - Banca Intesa Beograd, OTP Serbia, UniCredit Serbia, AIK Banka - an existing NCR recycler reference, NLB Komercijalna) keep operating under the existing eIDAS-1-style law, where remote onboarding rests on the NBS video-identification rules rather than on a wallet. Printec should position Namirial against the EXISTING NBS video-identification regime rather than a future wallet, and treat any eIDAS-2 bill appearing in 2027 as the next trigger.
signals.likelihood: Low - no bill identified; alignment is a Commission recommendation only
signals.followup: Search the Serbian Ministry of Information and Telecommunications and NBS local-language sites for an eIDAS-2 alignment bill, and re-check the NBS video-identification decision for any 2026 amendment.

signals.entity: Montenegro - Ministry of Public Administration; CBCG
signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2025] The European Commission's Montenegro Report 2025 states that 'Regarding electronic identification and trust services, Montenegro is encouraged to swiftly align its national legislation with the new EU Digital Identity and Trust Services framework' - i.e. Montenegro is NOT aligned with eIDAS 2 and no national wallet programme is recorded. The same chapter notes Montenegro is establishing a Cybersecurity Agency and working towards NIS2 requirements.
signals.implies: No wallet trigger in Montenegro. Given Montenegro's front-runner accession position, an eIDAS-2 alignment law is the realistic 2027 trigger; until then Printec's Montenegro plays (CKB/OTP, NLB Banka Podgorica, Erste Bank Podgorica, Hipotekarna, Universal Capital Bank) stay on cash automation, ATM estate and AML rather than eID. Watch the November-2026 Western Balkans TIPS-Clone onboarding window as the nearer trigger.
signals.followup: Check the Montenegrin Ministry of Public Administration and CBCG local-language pages for an eIDAS-2 alignment bill in the 2026-2027 legislative programme.

signals.entity: Republic of Albania - AKSHI / Bank of Albania
signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2025] The European Commission's Albania Report 2025 states that 'Albania should adopt the Law on electronic identification and trust services, to align with the European Digital Identity regulation' - i.e. as at 04/11/2025 Albania had NOT adopted an eIDAS-aligned eID/trust-services law, despite operating the e-Albania portal. The same chapter records the Cybersecurity Strategy 2025-2030 and Action Plan 2025-2027 as adopted and an updated list of operators of critical and important information infrastructure adopted in June 2025.
signals.implies: Albania's eID law is a pending, not a live, trigger. The dated Albanian obligation that DOES bite is the Bank of Albania Regulation on Digital Operational Resilience applying 01/07/2027, not eID. For OTP Albania and Raiffeisen Albania (existing Printec relationships) the eKYC conversation should be framed on BoA remote-onboarding rules and the e-Albania identity, with a wallet/eID law watch-item for 2027.
signals.likelihood: Medium - adoption is an explicit EU accession recommendation, so a bill in 2026-2027 is plausible
signals.followup: Check the Albanian Parliament (parlament.al) legislative calendar and AKSHI for a Law on electronic identification and trust services; bankofalbania.org needs a desktop User-Agent (it 403s to fetch tools).

signals.signal: A draft Law on the European Digital Identity Wallet (Zakon za Evropeyski portfeyl za tsifrova samolichnost) was reported published in FEBRUARY 2026, moving Bulgaria up the EUDI readiness rankings, but the assessment is that 'late-stage legal movement does not remove practical risk of late-stage technical delivery' against 24/12/2026. UNVERIFIED AGAINST A BULGARIAN PRIMARY SOURCE in this run: strategy.bg (the public consultations portal) presented a login wall and the WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted before a Bulgarian-language sweep could be completed. Treat the February-2026 date as aggregator-tier until the strategy.bg consultation record or the Darzhaven vestnik text is obtained.
signals.source_name: Namirial, 'EUDI Wallet: how prepared are the various EU countries?' (vendor status tracker, published 09/04/2026, last modified 06/08/2026)
signals.implies: If confirmed, Bulgaria is legislating for the wallet in the same window as euro adoption (01/01/2026 changeover completing 09/08/2026) and the contested 01/01/2027 instant-payments/VoP date - a stacked compliance year for UniCredit Bulbank, DSK, UBB, Postbank, Fibank and Allianz Bank Bulgaria in which eID work will compete for the same budget. Printec should sequence the Bulgarian pitch: euro/cash automation first, wallet RP registration and Namirial eKYC as the 2027 follow-on.

signals.followup: PRIORITY NEXT RUN: find the Bulgarian draft Law on the European Digital Identity Wallet on strategy.bg / the Ministry of e-Government site / parliament.bg, get its consultation and adoption dates, and check whether it names a registrar of wallet-relying parties.

signals.source_name: Namirial EUDI readiness tracker (vendor) and Biometric Update (press), citing ENISA and the Politecnico di Milano observatory

That asymmetry is Printec's opening: sell banks a wallet-agnostic RP acceptance layer plus Namirial eKYC that does not depend on any one national wallet shipping on time. Named targets: Alpha Bank and Piraeus/NBG/Eurobank (GR), Bank of Cyprus and Hellenic (CY), Slovenska sporitelna and VUB (SK), Ceska sporitelna and KB (CZ), NLB and Nova KBM (SI).

coverage_notes: Fresh run - no checkpoint existed for 27/08/2026. Covered: the EU implementing-act layer (CIR 2026/1731 full text, CIR 2026/798 remote onboarding, CIR 2025/848 relying-party registration), ARF v3.0.0, and every non-EU footprint market's eID/trust-services status via the European Commission's own 2025 Enlargement Package country reports (primary, downloaded and text-extracted locally). CARRIED DEBT (3) CLOSED: AUSTRIA - closed with a primary parliamentary source (State Secretary Proell, Budget Committee 29/06/2026: no member state will meet end-2026, Austria will implement incrementally; plus 5687/AB of 12/08/2026 where the Interior Ministry declines the file). CROATIA - PARTLY closed: Trusted List TLv6 migration 29/04/2026 confirmed primary on gov.hr, but no Croatian government wallet timetable exists; the Q4-2026 certified-wallet date remains press-tier only, and that limitation is stated in the row. NEW THIS RUN vs the 02/08/2026 baseline: ARF v3.0.0 (23/07/2026) with the conformance.eudi.dev test framework; the substance of CIR 2026/1731 (biometric-portrait warning Art.3a, EUDI trust mark Art.14a, Annex Ia cryptography, Annex Ib wallet unit attestation, CTAP 2.3, and a previously unrecorded 11/08/2028 mandatory-portrait date); CIR 2026/798 of 07/04/2026 on remote onboarding via ETSI TS 119 461 V2.1.1 - the act that legally enables remote eKYC into wallets and which the baseline did not carry; and CIR 2025/848 applying from 24/12/2026, which is the first EU date that bites on BANKS as relying parties, a full year before the widely-quoted 24/12/2027 Art.5f(2) acceptance date. North Macedonia's 01/06/2027 is upgraded from partially-confirmed to primary-confirmed AND the bill's Art.20-m(2) is shown expressly to name banking and financial services as relying parties that must accept the wallet on user request. GENUINE GAPS: (a) the per-country wallet status for Greece, Cyprus, Bulgaria, Romania, Hungary, Czechia, Slovakia and Slovenia rests on aggregator/vendor tracking only, and Bulgaria's reported February-2026 draft Law on the European Digital Identity Wallet is unverified against a Bulgarian primary source; (b) no Member State's designated REGISTER OF WALLET-RELYING PARTIES has been identified in the footprint, which is the single most useful next artefact; (c) the mandatory local-language sweep of national regulator news pages (BoG, CBC, BNR, BNB, MNB, CNB-CZ, NBS-SK, BSI, NBRNM, CBCG, NBS-RS, CBK, BoA, NBU) could NOT be completed. CAUSE: this session's WebSearch budget (200/200 calls) was exhausted mid-run by the wider orchestration; from that point only WebFetch and curl against known URLs were available, and both Google and DuckDuckGo returned CAPTCHA/anti-bot pages to fetch tools, so no substitute search route existed. Everything reported here was actually opened. Confidence is capped at Medium per the single-agent rule; aggregator-only rows are marked Low.
access_issues: eur-lex.europa.eu: HTTP 202 AWS WAF challenge to curl (full desktop User-Agent, Accept/Sec-Fetch headers, cookie jar) AND to WebFetch, on https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=OJ:L_202601731, .../?uri=OJ:L_202600798, and the ELI PDF routes /eli/reg_impl/2026/1731/oj/eng/pdf and CELEX:32026R1731. publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32026R1731 returned HTTP 400. ROUTE USED INSTEAD: a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) over the same EUR-Lex HTML URLs, which succeeded for 2026/1731, 2026/798 and 2025/848 - the content is EUR-Lex's, but the signed OJ PDF has NOT been verified, so exact OJ publication dates carry a to-be-confirmed flag. portal.mdt.gov.mk (North Macedonia Ministry for Digital Transformation) and ener.gov.mk: ECONNREFUSED from this network - the MK primary law text could not be opened; the MK bill was obtained instead from the Economic Chamber of North Macedonia mirror (mchamber.mk) and extracted locally with pdfminer, and corroborated with the Commission's own country report. slobodnaevropa.org: HTTP 403 to WebFetch. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EU_Digital_Identity_Wallet: HTTP 404. strategy.bg public-consultations portal: login wall. WebSearch: the session budget (200/200 calls) was exhausted partway through, before the Greek, Cypriot, Bulgarian, Romanian, Hungarian, Czech, Slovak and Slovenian local-language sweeps. Fallback search routes html.duckduckgo.com (HTTP 202 anti-bot), lite.duckduckgo.com (CAPTCHA) and google.com via reader proxy (unusual-traffic block) all failed, so no substitute search was possible. pdftotext is not installed on this machine; PDFs were extracted with pdfminer.six instead.
operator_requests: 1) Open the signed OJ PDFs in a browser and confirm exact OJ publication and entry-into-force dates for Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1731 (OJ L_202601731) and (EU) 2026/798 (OJ L_202600798) - EUR-Lex is WAF-blocked to automated fetch. 2) Retrieve the ADOPTED North Macedonian text of the Law amending the Law on Electronic Documents, Electronic Identification and Trusted Services from Sluzben vesnik na RSM (portal.mdt.gov.mk is unreachable from this network) and confirm Art.20-m(2) and the 01/06/2027 application date. 3) Retrieve the Bulgarian draft Law on the European Digital Identity Wallet from strategy.bg (the portal requires a login) or Darzhaven vestnik. 4) Raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION or re-run this workstream with a fresh search budget so the mandatory local-language regulator sweep can be completed. Nothing paywalled was encountered.
